sanskrit: etat sarvaṃ yathāvṛttaṃ śrotum icchāmi lomaśa karmabhir devakalpānāṃ kīrtyamānair bhṛśaṃ rame
english: I wish to hear all this, just as it occurred, O Lomaśa — I greatly delight in hearing the deeds of those who are like the gods being recounted.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca bharadvājaś ca raibhyaś ca sakhāyau saṃbabhūvatuḥ tāv ūṣatur ihātyantaṃ prīyamāṇau vanāntare
english: Lomaśa said: Bharadvāja and Raibhya were friends; those two dwelt here in the forest, greatly delighting in each other's company.

sanskrit: raibhyasya tu sutāv āstām arvāvasuparāvasū āsīd yavakrīḥ putras tu bharadvājasya bhārata
english: Raibhya had two sons, Arvāvasu and Paravasu; and Yavakrī was the son of Bharadvāja, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: raibhyo vidvān sahāpatyas tapasvī cetaro 'bhavat tayoś cāpy atulā prītir bālyāt prabhṛti bhārata
english: Raibhya was learned together with his sons, while the other was an ascetic; yet between those two there was incomparable affection from childhood onward, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yavakrīḥ pitaraṃ dṛṣṭvā tapasvinam asatkṛtam dṛṣṭvā ca satkṛtaṃ viprai raibhyaṃ putraiḥ sahānagha
english: Yavakrī, seeing his father the ascetic dishonored, and seeing Raibhya honored along with his sons by the brahmins, O sinless one —

sanskrit: paryatapyata tejasvī manyunābhipariplutaḥ tapas tepe tato ghoraṃ vedajñānāya pāṇḍava
english: — that brilliant one burned with grief, overwhelmed by anger, and then performed terrible austerities to attain knowledge of the Vedas, O Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: susamiddhe mahaty agnau śarīram upatāpayan janayām āsa saṃtāpam indrasya sumahātapāḥ
english: Torturing his body in a great blazing fire, that mighty ascetic generated intense anguish in Indra.

sanskrit: tata indro yavakrītam upagamya yudhiṣṭhira abravīt kasya hetos tvam āsthitas tapa uttamam
english: Then Indra approached Yavakrī, O Yudhiṣṭhira, and said: "For what reason have you undertaken this supreme austerity?"

sanskrit: yavakrīr uvāca dvijānām anadhītā vai vedāḥ suragaṇārcita pratibhāntv iti tapye 'ham idaṃ paramakaṃ tapaḥ
english: Yavakrī said: "May the Vedas, unlearned by twice-borns, shine forth in me" — O you worshipped by the host of gods, for this I perform this supreme austerity.

sanskrit: svādhyāyārthe samārambho mamāyaṃ pākaśāsana tapasā jñātum icchāmi sarvajñānāni kauśika
english: "This undertaking of mine is for the purpose of sacred recitation, O Indra, lord of the slayer of Pāka; I wish to know all knowledge through austerity, O Kauśika."

sanskrit: kālena mahatā vedāḥ śakyā gurumukhād vibho prāptuṃ tasmād ayaṃ yatnaḥ paramo me samāsthitaḥ
english: "The Vedas can be attained through a teacher's mouth only after a great length of time, O lord; therefore this supreme effort has been undertaken by me."

sanskrit: indra uvāca amārga eṣa viprarṣe yena tvaṃ yātum icchasi kiṃ vighātena te vipra gacchādhīhi guror mukhāt
english: Indra said: "This is a wrong path by which you wish to go, O brahmin-seer; what obstacle is there for you, O brahmin? Go and study from the mouth of a teacher."

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca evam uktvā gataḥ śakro yavakrīr api bhārata bhūya evākarod yatnaṃ tapasy amitavikrama
english: Lomaśa said: Having spoken thus, Śakra departed; and Yavakrī, O Bhārata, once again made effort in austerity, O one of immeasurable valor.

sanskrit: ghoreṇa tapasā rājaṃs tapyamāno mahātapāḥ saṃtāpayām āsa bhṛśaṃ devendram iti naḥ śrutam
english: Afflicting himself with terrible austerity, O king, that great ascetic greatly tormented the lord of the gods — so we have heard.

sanskrit: taṃ tathā tapyamānaṃ tu tapas tīvraṃ mahāmunim upetya balabhid devo vārayām āsa vai punaḥ
english: Then approaching that great sage performing such intense austerity, the god Balabhid once again tried to restrain him.

sanskrit: aśakyo 'rthaḥ samārabdho naitad buddhikṛtaṃ tava pratibhāsyanti vai vedās tava caiva pituś ca te
english: "The goal you have undertaken is unattainable; this is not a wise course for you — the Vedas will indeed shine forth in you and in your father."

sanskrit: yavakrīr uvāca na caitad evaṃ kriyate devarāja mamepsitam mahatā niyamenāhaṃ tapsye ghorataraṃ tapaḥ
english: Yavakrī said: "This desired goal of mine is not being accomplished thus, O king of gods; with great self-restraint I shall perform even more terrible austerity."

sanskrit: samiddhe 'gnāv upakṛtyāṅgam aṅgaṃ; hoṣyāmi vā maghavaṃs tan nibodha yady etad evaṃ na karoṣi kāmaṃ; mamepsitaṃ devarājeha sarvam
english: "I shall offer limb by limb into the blazing fire — know this, O Maghavan; if you do not grant all my desired wishes here, O king of gods."

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca niścayaṃ tam abhijñāya munes tasya mahātmanaḥ prativāraṇahetvarthaṃ buddhyā saṃcintya buddhimān
english: Lomaśa said: Recognizing the resolve of that great-souled sage, the wise one reflected with his intellect on a means to restrain him.

sanskrit: tata indro 'karod rūpaṃ brāhmaṇasya tapasvinaḥ anekaśatavarṣasya durbalasya sayakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Then Indra assumed the form of an ascetic brahmin many hundreds of years old, feeble and afflicted with consumption.

sanskrit: yavakrītasya yat tīrtham ucitaṃ śaucakarmaṇi bhāgīrathyāṃ tatra setuṃ vālukābhiś cakāra saḥ
english: At the tirtha on the Bhāgīrathī customarily used by Yavakrī for his purification rituals, he began to build a bridge with handfuls of sand.

sanskrit: yadāsya vadato vākyaṃ na sa cakre dvijottamaḥ vālukābhis tataḥ śakro gaṅgāṃ samabhipūrayan
english: When that foremost of twice-borns paid no heed to his words, Śakra then began filling the Gaṅgā with sand.

sanskrit: vālukāmuṣṭim aniśaṃ bhāgīrathyāṃ vyasarjayat setum abhyārabhac chakro yavakrītaṃ nidarśayan
english: He continuously cast handfuls of sand into the Bhāgīrathī and set about building the bridge, demonstrating this to Yavakrī.

sanskrit: taṃ dadarśa yavakrīs tu yatnavantaṃ nibandhane prahasaṃś cābravīd vākyam idaṃ sa munipuṃgavaḥ
english: Yavakrī saw him striving at this construction and laughing spoke these words, that bull among sages:

sanskrit: kim idaṃ vartate brahman kiṃ ca te ha cikīrṣitam atīva hi mahān yatnaḥ kriyate 'yaṃ nirarthakaḥ
english: "What is going on here, O brahmin, and what is it you intend to do? This is an exceedingly great effort being made, and it is pointless."

sanskrit: indra uvāca bandhiṣye setunā gaṅgāṃ sukhaḥ panthā bhaviṣyati kliśyate hi janas tāta taramāṇaḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: Indra said: "I shall bind the Gaṅgā with a bridge so that the path may be easy; for the people suffer greatly when they cross repeatedly, my child."

sanskrit: yavakrīr uvāca nāyaṃ śakyas tvayā baddhuṃ mahān oghaḥ kathaṃ cana aśakyād vinivartasva śakyam arthaṃ samārabha
english: Yavakrī said: "This mighty current cannot be bridged by you in any way; desist from the impossible and undertake a feasible task."

sanskrit: indra uvāca yathaiva bhavatā cedaṃ tapo vedārtham udyatam aśakyaṃ tadvad asmābhir ayaṃ bhāraḥ samudyataḥ
english: Indra said: "Just as this austerity undertaken by you to attain the Vedas is impossible, so likewise this burden has been undertaken by us."

sanskrit: yavakrīr uvāca yathā tava nirartho 'yam ārambhas tridaśeśvara tathā yadi mamāpīdaṃ manyase pākaśāsana
english: Yavakrī said: "If you consider my undertaking equally pointless, O lord of the thirty gods, O Pākaśāsana —

sanskrit: kriyatāṃ yad bhavec chakyaṃ mayā suragaṇeśvara varāṃś ca me prayacchānyān yair anyān bhavitāsmy ati
english: "— then grant what may be possible for me, O lord of the host of gods, and give me other boons by which I may surpass all others."

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca tasmai prādād varān indra uktavān yān mahātapāḥ pratibhāsyanti te vedāḥ pitrā saha yathepsitāḥ
english: Lomaśa said: To him Indra gave the boons that the great ascetic had declared: "The Vedas shall shine forth in you together with your father, as you desire."

sanskrit: yac cānyat kāṅkṣase kāmaṃ yavakrīr gamyatām iti sa labdhakāmaḥ pitaram upetyātha tato 'bravīt
english: "And whatever other wish you desire, Yavakrī, go to it." Having obtained his desire, he then approached his father and spoke.

sanskrit: yavakrīr uvāca pratibhāsyanti vai vedā mama tātasya cobhayoḥ ati cānyān bhaviṣyāvo varā labdhās tathā mayā
english: Yavakrī said: "The Vedas shall indeed shine forth in both me and my father; and the boons obtained by me shall likewise be beyond all others."

sanskrit: bharadvāja uvāca darpas te bhavitā tāta varāṃl labdhvā yathepsitān sa darpapūrṇaḥ kṛpaṇaḥ kṣipram eva vinaśyasi
english: Bharadvāja said: "Arrogance will come upon you, my child, having obtained the boons you desired; filled with that arrogance, the wretched one perishes quickly."

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmā gāthā devair udāhṛtāḥ ṛṣir āsīt purā putra bāladhir nāma vīryavān
english: "On this point they cite these verses, declared by the gods: In ancient times, my son, there was a powerful sage named Baladhi."

sanskrit: sa putraśokād udvignas tapas tepe suduścaram bhaven mama suto 'martya iti taṃ labdhavāṃś ca saḥ
english: "Distressed by grief for a son, he performed extremely difficult austerities, and he obtained this boon: that his son would be immortal."

sanskrit: tasya prasādo devaiś ca kṛto na tv amaraiḥ samaḥ nāmartyo vidyate martyo nimittāyur bhaviṣyati
english: "A boon was granted to him by the gods, yet not equal to the immortals: 'No mortal is immortal; your mortal son shall have a conditioned lifespan.'"

sanskrit: bāladhir uvāca yatheme parvatāḥ śaśvat tiṣṭhanti surasattamāḥ akṣayās tan nimittaṃ me sutasyāyur bhaved iti
english: "Baladhi said: 'As these mountains stand forever, O best of gods, inexhaustible — let the mountains be the condition of my son's lifespan.'"

sanskrit: bharadvāja uvāca tasya putras tadā jajñe medhāvī krodhanaḥ sadā sa tac chrutvākarod darpam ṛṣīṃś caivāvamanyata
english: "Bharadvāja said: A son was then born to him, named Medhāvī, always wrathful; hearing this boon, he became arrogant and began to disrespect the sages."

sanskrit: vikurvāṇo munīnāṃ tu caramāṇo mahīm imām āsasāda mahāvīryaṃ dhanuṣākṣaṃ manīṣiṇam
english: "While acting wrongfully toward the sages and roaming this earth, he encountered the wise and mighty Dhanusha-ksha."

sanskrit: tasyāpacakre medhāvī taṃ śaśāpa sa vīryavān bhava bhasmeti coktaḥ sa na bhasma samapadyata
english: "Medhāvī insulted him; that powerful one cursed him: 'Become ashes!' But when so spoken to, he did not become ashes."

sanskrit: dhanuṣākṣas tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā medhāvinam anāmayam nimittam asya mahiṣair bhedayām āsa vīryavān
english: "But Dhanuṣākṣa, seeing Medhāvī unharmed, that powerful one shattered the conditioned support of his life with buffaloes."

sanskrit: sa nimitte vinaṣṭe tu mamāra sahasā śiśuḥ taṃ mṛtaṃ putram ādāya vilalāpa tataḥ pitā
english: "When the conditional support was destroyed, the child suddenly died; and taking up that dead son, his father then lamented."

sanskrit: lālapyamānaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā munayaḥ punar ārtavat ūcur vedoktayā pūrvaṃ gāthayā tan nibodha me
english: "Seeing him lamenting in such pain, the sages spoke again with a verse taught in the Vedas — hear this from me."

sanskrit: na diṣṭam artham atyetum īśo martyaḥ kathaṃ cana mahiṣair bhedayām āsa dhanuṣākṣo mahīdharān
english: "No mortal is ever able to transcend fate in any way; Dhanuṣākṣa shattered the mountains with his buffaloes."

sanskrit: evaṃ labdhvā varān bālā darpapūrṇās tarasvinaḥ kṣipram eva vinaśyanti yathā na syāt tathā bhavān
english: "Thus, children who obtain boons and are filled with arrogance, however swift, perish quickly — may you not be so, my son."

sanskrit: eṣa raibhyo mahāvīryaḥ putrau cāsya tathāvidhau taṃ yathā putra nābhyeṣi tathā kuryās tv atandritaḥ
english: "This Raibhya is greatly powerful and his sons are likewise; act diligently so that you do not approach him, my son."

sanskrit: sa hi kruddhaḥ samarthas tvāṃ putra pīḍayituṃ ruṣā vaidyaś cāpi tapasvī ca kopanaś ca mahān ṛṣiḥ
english: "For when angered, he is capable of harming you in his wrath, my son — he is a physician, an ascetic, and a great irascible sage."

sanskrit: yavakrīr uvāca evaṃ kariṣye mā tāpaṃ tāta kārṣīḥ kathaṃ cana yathā hi me bhavān mānyas tathā raibhyaḥ pitā mama
english: Yavakrī said: "I shall act accordingly; do not grieve in any way, father; for just as you are to be honored by me, so Raibhya is as a father to me."

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca uktvā sa pitaraṃ ślakṣṇaṃ yavakrīr akutobhayaḥ viprakurvann ṛṣīn anyān atuṣyat parayā mudā
english: Lomaśa said: Having spoken smoothly to his father, Yavakrī, fearless, went on wronging other sages and rejoiced with great delight.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca caṅkramyamāṇaḥ sa tadā yavakrīr akutobhayaḥ jagāma mādhave māsi raibhyāśramapadaṃ prati
english: Lomaśa said: Wandering about at that time, fearless Yavakrī went in the month of Mādhava toward the hermitage of Raibhya.

sanskrit: sa dadarśāśrame puṇye puṣpitadrumabhūṣite vicarantīṃ snuṣāṃ tasya kiṃnarīm iva bhārata
english: In that holy hermitage adorned with flowering trees, he saw Raibhya's daughter-in-law roaming about, like a kinnari, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yavakrīs tām uvācedam upatiṣṭhasva mām iti nirlajjo lajjayā yuktāṃ kāmena hṛtacetanaḥ
english: Yavakrī said to her, "Yield to me" — shameless, his mind stolen by desire, to her who was full of modesty.

sanskrit: sā tasya śīlam ājñāya tasmāc chāpāc ca bibhyatī tejasvitāṃ ca raibhyasya tathety uktvā jagāma sā
english: She, knowing his character and fearing the curse from him and the fierce energy of Raibhya, saying "So be it," went with him.

sanskrit: tata ekāntam unnīya majjayām āsa bhārata ājagāma tadā raibhyaḥ svam āśramam ariṃdama
english: Then, having led her to a secluded spot, he defiled her, O Bhārata; and then Raibhya came to his own hermitage, O subduer of enemies.

sanskrit: rudantīṃ ca snuṣāṃ dṛṣṭvā bhāryām ārtāṃ parāvasoḥ tathā sāntvayañ ślakṣṇayā vācā paryapṛcchad yudhiṣṭhira
english: Seeing his daughter-in-law weeping, the distressed wife of Paravasu, he comforted her with gentle words and inquired of her, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: sā tasmai sarvam ācaṣṭa yavakrībhāṣitaṃ śubhā pratyuktaṃ ca yavakrītaṃ prekṣāpūrvaṃ tadātmanā
english: That auspicious woman told him everything — what Yavakrī had said and what reply Yavakrī had received beforehand from her own self.

sanskrit: śṛṇvānasyaiva raibhyasya yavakrītaviceṣṭitam dahann iva tadā cetaḥ krodhaḥ samabhavan mahān
english: Even as Raibhya was hearing of Yavakrī's conduct, a mighty anger arose in his heart, burning as if with fire.

sanskrit: sa tadā manyunāviṣṭas tapasvī bhṛśakopanaḥ avalupya jaṭām ekāṃ juhāvāgnau susaṃskṛte
english: Then that ascetic, seized by fury and intensely enraged, plucked out one of his matted locks and offered it into the well-consecrated fire.

sanskrit: tataḥ samabhavan nārī tasyā rūpeṇa saṃmitā avalupyāparāṃ cātha juhāvāgnau jaṭāṃ punaḥ
english: From that arose a woman matching the beauty of that daughter-in-law; and plucking another matted lock, he offered it into the fire again.

sanskrit: tataḥ samabhavad rakṣo ghorākṣaṃ bhīmadarśanam abrūtāṃ tau tadā raibhyaṃ kiṃ kāryaṃ karavāmahe
english: From that arose a demon with terrible eyes and a frightful appearance; those two then said to Raibhya, "What task shall we perform?"

sanskrit: tāv abravīd ṛṣiḥ kruddho yavakrīr vadhyatām iti jagmatus tau tathety uktvā yavakrītajighāṃsayā
english: The enraged sage said to them: "Let Yavakrī be slain." Those two said "So be it" and went with intent to kill Yavakrī.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ samupāsthāya kṛtyā sṛṣṭā mahātmanā kamaṇḍaluṃ jahārāsya mohayitvā tu bhārata
english: Then the female demon sent by that great soul approached him and, having deluded him, stole his water-pot, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: ucchiṣṭaṃ tu yavakrītam apakṛṣṭakamaṇḍalum tata udyataśūlaḥ sa rākṣasaḥ samupādravat
english: With Yavakrī thus defiled and his water-pot taken away, then the demon with upraised spear rushed at him.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya śūlahastaṃ jighāṃsayā yavakrīḥ sahasotthāya prādravad yena vai saraḥ
english: Seeing him rushing at him with spear in hand intent on killing, Yavakrī instantly rose up and fled toward a lake.

sanskrit: jalahīnaṃ saro dṛṣṭvā yavakrīs tvaritaḥ punaḥ jagāma saritaḥ sarvās tāś cāpy āsan viśoṣitāḥ
english: Seeing the lake waterless, Yavakrī hurried on; he went to all the rivers, and those too had been dried up.

sanskrit: sa kālyamāno ghoreṇa śūlahastena rakṣasā agnihotraṃ pitur bhītaḥ sahasā samupādravat
english: Being driven by the terrible demon with the spear in hand, in fear he suddenly rushed toward his father's sacred fire.

sanskrit: sa vai praviśamānas tu śūdreṇāndhena rakṣiṇā nigṛhīto balād dvāri so 'vātiṣṭhata pārthiva
english: But as he was entering, he was forcibly seized by the blind shudra guardian at the gate, and he stood stopped there, O king.

sanskrit: nigṛhītaṃ tu śūdreṇa yavakrītaṃ sa rākṣasaḥ tāḍayām āsa śūlena sa bhinnahṛdayo 'patat
english: The demon then struck with the spear Yavakrī who was seized by the shudra; his heart pierced, he fell.

sanskrit: yavakrītaṃ sa hatvā tu rākṣaso raibhyam āgamat anujñātas tu raibhyeṇa tayā nāryā sahācarat
english: Having killed Yavakrī, the demon came back to Raibhya; dismissed by Raibhya, he went away accompanied by that woman.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca bharadvājas tu kaunteya kṛtvā svādhyāyam āhnikam samitkalāpam ādāya praviveśa svam āśramam
english: Lomaśa said: Bharadvāja, O son of Kuntī, having completed his daily recitation, took up his bundle of firewood and entered his own hermitage.

sanskrit: taṃ sma dṛṣṭvā purā sarve pratyuttiṣṭhanti pāvakāḥ na tv enam upatiṣṭhanti hataputraṃ tadāgnayaḥ
english: The sacred fires, which formerly all rose to greet him upon his arrival, did not attend upon him now that his son was slain.

sanskrit: vaikṛtaṃ tv agnihotre sa lakṣayitvā mahātapāḥ tam andhaṃ śūdram āsīnaṃ gṛhapālam athābravīt
english: Perceiving the disorder in the sacred fire-ritual, that great ascetic then spoke to the blind shudra sitting there as guardian of the household.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu me nāgnayaḥ śūdra pratinandanti darśanam tvaṃ cāpi na yathāpūrvaṃ kaccit kṣemam ihāśrame
english: "Why do the fires not welcome my arrival, O shudra? And you too are not as before — is all well in this hermitage?"

sanskrit: kaccin na raibhyaṃ putro me gatavān alpacetanaḥ etad ācakṣva me śīghraṃ na hi me śudhyate manaḥ
english: "Has my son of little understanding gone to Raibhya? Tell me this quickly, for my mind is not at peace."

sanskrit: śūdra uvāca raibhyaṃ gato nūnam asau sutas te mandacetanaḥ tathā hi nihataḥ śete rākṣasena balīyasā
english: The shudra said: "Your son of dull understanding has surely gone to Raibhya — for indeed he lies slain by a powerful demon."

sanskrit: prakālyamānas tenāyaṃ śūlahastena rakṣasā agnyāgāraṃ prati dvāri mayā dorbhyāṃ nivāritaḥ
english: "As he was being driven by that demon with spear in hand toward the fire-chamber, at the gate he was restrained by me with my arms."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa nihato hy atra jalakāmo 'śucir dhruvam saṃbhāvito hi tūrṇena śūlahastena rakṣasā
english: "Then he was killed here, for he was surely impure, thirsting for water, struck quickly by the demon with the upraised spear."

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca bharadvājas tu śūdrasya tac chrutvā vipriyaṃ vacaḥ gatāsuṃ putram ādāya vilalāpa suduḥkhitaḥ
english: Lomaśa said: Bharadvāja, hearing those unwelcome words of the shudra, took up his son who had breathed his last and lamented in deep sorrow.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇānāṃ kilārthāya nanu tvaṃ taptavāṃs tapaḥ dvijānām anadhītā vai vedāḥ saṃpratibhāntv iti
english: "Indeed you performed austerities for the sake of the brahmins — 'May the Vedas, unlearned by twice-borns, now shine forth' — so you said."
